design.scope: Hashed provider/config/auth context; observable credential generation and confidence
design.manualRefresh: Uses the same cache and cooldown; no bypass
design.timestamps: Preserves original lastAttempt and lastSuccess across processes
design.coordination: Exclusive OS-owned 127.0.0.1 socket per hashed cache namespace; no lockfile reaping
design.publication: Private atomic JSON via the existing durable-file helper; attempt marker precedes transport invocation
design.privacy: Normalized usage, safe error codes, timestamps and hashes only. No credential contents or raw provider responses persisted.

alternatives.decision: Rejected because stale takeover and release can remove a replacement owner.
Rejected because the existing readers can coordinate without another process or service.
Selected to keep cached data durable and lock ownership tied to the operating system.

review.intent: Reduce duplicate provider polling across Pi processes without marking cached data newly fetched.
corrected: Success expiry aligned with attempt start to avoid skipping the next five-minute monitor tick.
Added source-verified Codex auth selectors and corrected native Antigravity state path.
Opaque contexts cannot retain stale values beyond five minutes, including legacy cooldown/error records.
Mid-read scope changes discard results rather than publishing under a new context.
limitations: All running Pi instances need the updated extension; older versions and other provider clients do not cooperate.
Known identity means an observable local credential context, not universal proof for every OS keyring backend.
A five-minute durable attempt marker limits crash retries but does not guarantee containment of arbitrary orphaned external CLIs.
Port or storage failures fail closed; no uncached bypass.
The atomic publication helper has bounded synchronous Windows retry and does not promise power-loss durability.
